thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: HIGH: Elevated 5xx/latency observed in us-west-2 affecting Hosted API + several Dedicated pools. Auto-pager: @alex (oncall)

alex: I'm on it. seeing spike in 502/504 from us-west-2 edge. hitting Hosted API regional ELBs and two dedicated GPU pools in the region.

maya: confirmed from infra side — AWS ELB health checks flapping, target group 5xx > 30% in the last 3m. CloudWatch logs show downstream 5xx from aws-api-gateway and STS errors.

tom: tagging routing team. can we start routing traffic away from us-west-2 to us-east-1 as a short-term mitigation? need to consider cache warming + cold starts risk.

katie: customer-impact: multiple in-flight Hosted API requests are timing out; some Dedicated customers in us-west-2 hit higher latency and tokenized billing spikes. prep support comms if we need to mention degraded regional service.

support-lead: support queue already getting six tickets referencing 5xx in us-west. please call out any impacted customers on reserved Dedicated contracts.

alex: doing quick triage steps: 1) pause new canary deploys to us-west-2 (deploy-bot, hold) 2) flip smart-routing policy to prefer us-east-1 for new traffic 3) scale up fallback model variants in other regions 4) escalate to AWS if control plane errors persist.

deploy-bot: Deploys paused for cluster: rw-hosted-us-west-2 (user request alex).

maya: running commands now:
```
# list ELB target group 5xx
aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-west-2:... | jq '.TargetHealthDescriptions[] | {Target: .Target.Id, State: .TargetHealth.State, Reason: .TargetHealth.Reason}'
```
Results: ~40% unhealthy, reason: HTTPCode_Target_5XX_Error.

ops: observed STS throttling spikes — auth calls to sts.amazonaws.com are returning 500/503 intermittently which causes our auth proxy to cascade 502s to clients. Looks like a regional AWS control-plane degradation.

alex: ok, immediate mitigation plan:
- set smart-routing override: route-hosted: prefer=us-east-1, fallback=eu-west-1 (quick config push)
- shift Dedicated customer pools >= critical tier to reserved cross-region capacity (manually attach to us-east)
- enable prefix/KV cache warmup in us-east for top 5 model keys to reduce cold-start token pressure
- disable non-essential analytics writes to observability pipeline from us-west to reduce downstream pressure

maya: making the routing override now. pushing to console and will monitor propagation.

(1m later)
maya: override pushed — routing keys showing ~60% of new requests now going to us-east-1. latency on new requests trending down for Hosted API.

support-lead: notify affected Dedicated customers? recommend controlled notification: "We are experiencing elevated errors in AWS us-west-2 due to a regional provider issue. We’ve routed traffic to other regions and expect degraded performance to subside. No action required on your side unless you are pinned to us-west-2."

katie: agreed — publish status page note in 10 minutes if stabilized. include mitigation steps and ETA unknown.

alex: long-term investigation items: check STS token refresh backoff logic to avoid generating more auth calls during a provider flap; add circuit-breaker to auth proxy; add per-region auth call queuing.

ops: also we should temporarily reduce sampling rate to Datadog/observability from us-west to avoid thundering writes — that will help our control plane.

maya: reduced observability ingestion 80% for affected AZs. metric retention adjusted.

(10m later)

incident-bot: Incident severity remains sev2 — ongoing. Paging suspended for now while oncall monitors.

alex: seeing 5xx drop from 35% -> 6% over last 8m. latency 95p for hosted down from 2.8s -> 1.1s after reroute. Dedicated pool queuing reduced.

support-lead: triage notes for postmortem: timeline of AWS control-plane errors, routing override timestamp, affected customers, communications, oncall handoffs (alex -> tom in 30m), config changes (routing override id #rw-2245), analytics sampling reduction.

tom: I'll take next shift. alex, leave any open commands you want me to follow.

alex: handoff to tom in 30. leaving runbook steps in #sre-runbooks: runbook id rw-auth-fallback-v1. key steps we did are logged here:
- routing override applied 2245123512
- deploys paused 2245123520
- obs ingestion reduced 2245123601

ops: AWS console shows partial recovery; ELB target health improving but still noisy. We should keep routing override for another hour and then test gradual rollback.

katie: scheduling a customer ops sync at +45m to confirm no escalation.

(35m later)

tom: taking over. continuing to watch metrics. will coordinate rollback plan: gradual 10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% back to us-west, observe for 5xx regression for 5m at each step.

support-lead: filed the initial status page update and customer emails (no-PII).

alex: thanks team — thanks for quick response. follow-up: postmortem to include recommendations for cross-region auth caching, circuit-breaker on STS, and improving our routing fallback test coverage.

incident-bot: Incident resolved -> downgrading to sev3 at 2245126789.
